title: Tenali and the Magic Mango Tree
summary: A wandering ascetic named Siddha Govinda arrived in Vijayanagara, boasting in the marketplace that he possessed a 'Miraculous Mango Seed'...
keywords: tenali and the magic mango tree
full_text:
A wandering ascetic named Siddha Govinda arrived in Vijayanagara, boasting in the marketplace that he possessed a 'Miraculous Mango Seed' blessed by Himalayan hermits.
'Plant this seed in the ground,' he boasted, 'chant my secret mantra, and within one hour it will sprout, grow into a mature tree, blossom, and bear sweet ripe mangoes before your eyes! But beware: the tree will only grow for a man whose heart is free from every trace of foolishness!'

King Krishnadevaraya, intrigued by the claim, invited the ascetic to the palace gardens to perform the miracle before the court.

The ascetic dug a small hole in the lawn, placed a dried mango seed inside, covered it with soil, and sprinkled scented water.
He then turned to the King and said:
'Now, Maharaj, you must step forward and chant the sacred syllable. But remember: if you have ever committed a single foolish act in your life, the seed will rot and never sprout!'

The King hesitated, feeling uneasy: 'As a ruler, I have made hasty decisions in my youth. I cannot claim never to have been foolish.'
The ascetic turned to the Prime Minister, Appaji:
'Then let the Prime Minister chant!'
Appaji smiled wryly: 'Alas, I once bought a broken boat from a merchant; I, too, am not completely free of folly.'
One by one, the ministers and courtiers stepped back, confessing past mistakes.

The ascetic smirked triumphantly, preparing to collect his bag of gold for proving the court unworthy.
At that moment, Tenali Raman stepped forward:
'Give me the watering cup! I shall chant the mantra, for I have never committed a single foolish act in my life!'

The courtiers gasped. Tenali poured the water, chanted loudly, and waited.
One hour passed. Two hours passed. The sun climbed high.
The ground remained completely flat and bare: not a single green shoot appeared!

The ascetic sneered: 'Aha! Tenali Raman, thou hast lied! Thou art a fool, for the seed refused to sprout!'

Tenali laughed with booming joy:
'Indeed, friend ascetic! I was foolish enough to stand in the hot sun for two hours waiting for a dry mango seed to turn into a tree in sixty minutes!
And every courtier here was foolish enough to believe that nature violates its eternal seasons for your empty chant!
Trees require fertile soil, regular watering, patient months of sunlight, and honest labor to bear fruit. Whosoever expects sweet mangoes without honest farming is the greatest fool of all!'

The King and the ministers burst into laughter at Tenali’s brilliant demonstration.
The charlatan ascetic packed his dry seeds and fled the city, while the King planted real mango saplings in the royal orchards, learning that patient nature outshines all fraudulent shortcuts.
moral: Those who boast of supernatural miracles to justify laziness are humbled when confronted with natural reality.
